headline: THE 2-PRIMARY GLUING SEES BEYOND THE SPECTRUM, AND THE EDGE ACTION IS SIGNED.  On the cospectral family T(8), Chang(matching), Chang(8-cycle) the 2-primary eigenlattice gluing is (Z/2)^6 (+) (Z/4) for T(8) and (Z/2)^7 (+) (Z/4) for both Chang graphs: it separates T(8) from them, so it carries information no spectral invariant can, though it does not separate the two Chang graphs and is therefore not complete.  This is the payoff of the p = 2 case Pass 983 located as where the content sits.  Separately, Pass 983's open item is resolved: K commutes with the SIGNED oriented-edge action of Aut(W(3,3)) in 8 of 8 sampled automorphisms and with the unsigned action in 0 of 8, so the earlier negative result was an artefact of the wrong action.

part_A_separation.reading: The three graphs are cospectral, so no spectral invariant distinguishes them; the 2-primary gluing is (Z/2)^6 (+) (Z/4) for T(8) and (Z/2)^7 (+) (Z/4) for both Chang graphs, so it separates T(8) from them and carries information the spectrum does not.  It does not separate the two Chang graphs from each other, so it is finer than the spectrum but not complete.

part_B_signed_action.reading: With the signed oriented-edge action, K commutes with all eight sampled automorphisms; with the unsigned action it commutes with none.  Aut(W(3,3)) acts on the oriented edge space by signed permutation matrices that commute with K.
part_B_signed_action.resolves: Pass 983's open item: the earlier negative result used an unsigned permutation and was an artefact

open: the ramified p = 2 coalescence theorem itself
whether the gluing separates the two Chang graphs by some finer reading (it does not at the 2-primary level)
conjugacy classification of A5 in Aut(W(3,3)) (GAP absent in this environment)
part_C_boundary.scope: separation exhibited on one cospectral family of three graphs; commutation verified on eight sampled automorphisms, not proved for the whole group
